docs.title: voxbridge
docs.text: voxbridge is a Python SDK that puts one typed VoiceClient over the Vapi and Retell voice-agent platforms. Create agents, place outbound calls, verify and parse webhooks, and answer tool calls with the same code on either provider; switching is a config string.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
Voice-agent platforms diverge on nearly everything: endpoint prefixes, where the system prompt lives, webhook envelopes, signature schemes, voice-id formats. voxbridge absorbs those differences behind one small surface:

  • One API, many providers: agents, calls, tools and webhooks through a single VoiceClient.
  • Typed domain models: Pydantic v2 Agent, Call and Tool; every model keeps the untouched provider payload under .raw.
  • Normalized webhooks: each provider's envelope maps to one WebhookEvent union, with per-provider signature verification.
  • Sync and async: every agent/call method has an a-prefixed async twin.
  • No silent gaps: a capability a provider lacks raises NotSupported.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install voxbridge-sdk

Requires Python 3.12+. Runtime dependencies are httpx and pydantic only. The distribution is named voxbridge-sdk; the package you import is voxbridge.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
Provider-agnostic entry point: same API regardless of backend.

Requests are retried at most once. Connect errors, connect timeouts and 429 responses are retried for any request; read/write timeouts, 500/502/503/504 responses and other request errors only for idempotent requests. A Retry-After header is honoured, capped at 10 seconds. Capabilities a provider lacks raise NotSupported.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

First release, published on PyPI as voxbridge-sdk (import name voxbridge).

First release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• VoiceClient, one typed facade over Vapi and Retell, with sync methods and a-prefixed async twins, selected by a provider string.
  • Agent create, update, get and delete; outbound calls (create_call, get_call, list_calls(limit=...)); Pydantic Agent, Call and Tool models that keep the provider payload under .raw.
  • Define-once Tool registration that maps to each provider's native tool shape, and tool_response to build the reply a provider expects for a tool call.
  • Normalized webhooks: parse_webhook and verify_signature map both providers to one WebhookEvent union (CallStarted, CallEnded, TranscriptChunk, ToolCall, ErrorEvent), with per-provider signature verification.
  • VoiceClient.from_env() reading VOICE_PROVIDER, <P>_API_KEY, <P>_WEBHOOK_SECRET and <P>_WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE; a timeout option (default 30 s).
  • Error hierarchy: VoxBridgeError, ProviderError (status_code, body), AuthError, RateLimited (retry_after), NotSupported, SignatureError.
  • NotSupported for every capability gap instead of silent no-ops.
  • Retell: webhooks verified by default with the API key (or webhook_secret), with a 300 second replay window (webhook_max_age).
  • Vapi: Authorization: Bearer <secret> accepted alongside X-Vapi-Secret; E.164 from_number resolved to a phone-number id.
  • Docs site (MkDocs Material), README, configuration, webhooks and providers guides, runnable FastAPI and quickstart examples, CI matrix and trusted-publisher release workflow.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Vapi tool calls now parse the real nested function.name / function.arguments shape (arguments as object or JSON string); previously name came back empty.
  • Vapi update_agent merges onto the existing assistant instead of replacing settings voxbridge does not model.
  • Retell get_agent and update_agent read and write the agent's LLM, so the prompt, greeting, model and tools are no longer dropped; update_agent raises NotSupported for non-retell-llm agents.
  • Retell create_agent deletes the LLM it created if agent creation fails.
  • Retell list_calls now reads the v3 items envelope; Retell voice ids round-trip through the canonical "<tts-provider>:<voiceId>" form (elevenlabs becomes 11labs).
  • Retell custom-function requests parse to ToolCall.
  • Retell create_call raises ValueError up front when from_number is missing.
  • Retries: only idempotent requests are retried on read/write timeouts and 500/502/503/504 responses; connect errors, connect timeouts and 429s are retried for any request; Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date) is honoured, capped at 10 seconds.
  • Passing webhook_max_age for Vapi raises NotSupported instead of being ignored; from_env rejects an unknown provider before reading other variables.
  • Malformed webhook bodies raise ProviderError rather than a bare decode error.
  • update_agent keeps per-tool provider settings (Vapi server secret and headers, Retell headers and timeouts) for tools it re-sends.
  • Retell create_agent / update_agent raise ValueError up front for a tool without endpoint_url.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
from voxbridge import VoiceClient

client = VoiceClient(
    provider="retell",
    api_key="key_...",
    webhook_secret="key_...",   # optional
    webhook_max_age=300,        # Retell only, optional
    timeout=30,                 # optional
)
Argument Default Meaning provider required "vapi" or "retell"; anything else raises ValueError. api_key required The provider API key, sent as Authorization: Bearer. webhook_secret none Secret used to verify webhooks. On Vapi, leaving it unset means webhooks are not verified. On Retell it falls back to the API key. webhook_max_age 300 (Retell) Retell only. Maximum age of a webhook signature in seconds; None disables the replay check. Passing it for Vapi raises NotSupported, because Vapi signatures carry no timestamp. timeout 30 Per-request HTTP timeout in seconds.

docs.title: From the environment
docs.text:
VoiceClient.from_env() reads:

Variable Used for VOICE_PROVIDER Provider name (skipped if you pass provider=). VAPI_API_KEY / RETELL_API_KEY api_key. Required unless you pass api_key=. VAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET / RETELL_WEBHOOK_SECRET webhook_secret. RETELL_WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE webhook_max_age, a number. Setting VAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_AGE raises NotSupported.

Empty values count as unset. A missing provider or key, an unknown provider, or a non-numeric max age raises ValueError with a message naming the variable.

VoiceClient.from_env()                       # provider from VOICE_PROVIDER
VoiceClient.from_env("vapi")                 # explicit provider
VoiceClient.from_env("retell", timeout=60)   # keyword overrides win over the environment
VoiceClient.from_env("vapi", api_key=key)    # key from elsewhere; VAPI_API_KEY not needed
VoiceClient.from_env(environ={"VOICE_PROVIDER": "vapi", "VAPI_API_KEY": "sk-..."})  # custom mapping

docs.title: Where the variables come from
docs.text:
voxbridge reads os.environ and nothing else; it does not load .env files. Either export the variables in your shell or deployment platform, or load a .env yourself before building the client with python-dotenv:

from dotenv import load_dotenv

from voxbridge import VoiceClient

load_dotenv()                  # copies .env entries into os.environ
client = VoiceClient.from_env()

python-dotenv is not a voxbridge dependency; install it yourself (pip install python-dotenv). Keep .env out of version control.

docs.title: Retell webhook key
docs.text: Retell signs webhooks with an API key that carries the webhook badge in the Retell dashboard. When you don't pass a webhook_secret, voxbridge verifies with api_key, which only works if that key is the badged one. If your API key is not badged, pass the badged key as webhook_secret (or set RETELL_WEBHOOK_SECRET).

docs.title: Providers
docs.text: voxbridge supports two providers, selected by the provider string passed to VoiceClient: "vapi" and "retell".

docs.title: Capability matrix
docs.text:
Capability Vapi Retell Notes Agent create / update / get / delete yes yes Retell create is 2 API calls (LLM, then agent); update is 2 writes Outbound call yes yes create_call(agent_id, to_number, from_number=...); pass a caller from_number on both (Retell raises ValueError without it) Get call / list calls yes yes Default list size: Vapi 100, Retell 50; pass limit= Transcript on call yes yes Retell list_calls items carry none; use get_call Webhook events yes yes Normalized to one WebhookEvent union Webhook verification optional always Vapi only if you set a secret Signature scheme shared secret / Bearer HMAC-SHA256 X-Vapi-Secret vs x-retell-signature Replay protection no yes Vapi's scheme has no timestamp; Retell webhook_max_age (300 s) Tool round trip yes yes tool_response shapes the reply per provider Sync + async yes yes a-prefixed twins for agent/call methods; webhook helpers are sync

Anything a provider lacks raises NotSupported; voxbridge never no-ops silently.

docs.title: Voice ids
docs.text: Write voices as "<tts-provider>:<voiceId>", for example "elevenlabs:rachel" or "openai:alloy". elevenlabs is normalized to 11labs. Vapi receives {provider, voiceId}; Retell receives "<provider>-<voiceId>" (11labs-Adrian). Reading an agent back returns the canonical "<provider>:<voiceId>" form. A bare voice id with no colon is sent through unchanged on Retell and treated as ElevenLabs on Vapi. The catalogs differ: a voice that exists on one platform may not exist on the other, so the same string is not guaranteed to work on both.

docs.title: Call.from_number
docs.text: On Vapi, Call.from_number holds the Vapi phone-number id, because Vapi's call object doesn't echo the number. When you pass an E.164 from_number to create_call, voxbridge looks it up in your Vapi phone numbers and sends the id (ProviderError if none matches); a value not starting with + is sent as an id. The lookup reads one page of GET /phone-number (Vapi's default page size), so pass the phone-number id directly if your account has many numbers. On Retell it is the number itself.

docs.title: Retell list_calls has no transcript
docs.text: Items returned by Retell's list endpoint carry no transcript, so Call.transcript is None there. Call get_call(call_id) for the full call.

docs.title: Retell agents are two objects
docs.text:
Retell keeps the prompt, greeting, model and tools on a separate LLM object that the agent references. voxbridge handles both, with these consequences:

  • create_agent rollback. If creating the agent fails after the LLM was created, voxbridge deletes that LLM and re-raises the original error. Caveat: if the create-agent request timed out but Retell actually created the agent, the rollback deletes an LLM that the live agent points to. After a timeout on create, check your agent list.
  • update_agent is two writes, LLM first and then the agent. If the agent PATCH fails after the LLM PATCH succeeded, the LLM change stays; there is no rollback.
  • update_agent edits the LLM in place. If several agents share one Retell LLM, updating one changes them all.
  • Non-retell-llm agents. Agents whose response engine is not retell-llm (for example conversation flow) raise NotSupported on update_agent, and get_agent returns an empty prompt and model for them.

docs.title: update_agent semantics
docs.text: update_agent overlays your Agent on the existing one and keeps provider settings voxbridge doesn't model (voice stability, Vapi non-function tools, Retell built-in tools such as end_call). Because unset means "leave alone", update_agent cannot clear the greeting (first_message=None) or remove all tools in 0.1.0. When tools is non-empty it sets the custom function tools to exactly that list and keeps the built-ins. A tool whose name matches one already on the agent keeps its provider-only settings (Vapi server.secret, server.headers, async; Retell headers, query_params, method, response_variables, speak_*, timeout_ms); voxbridge only overwrites the name, description, parameters and URL. On Vapi, a model provider set outside voxbridge (for example groq) is kept while the model name is unchanged, and voice settings are kept while the voice provider is unchanged; switching voice provider starts a fresh voice block.

docs.title: Retell tools need a URL
docs.text: Retell calls a custom tool at its URL, so every Tool passed to Retell create_agent / update_agent needs endpoint_url. A tool without one raises ValueError("Retell custom tools require endpoint_url: <name>") before any request is sent. On Vapi, a tool without endpoint_url uses the assistant's server URL.

docs.title: Webhook authentication
docs.text: Retell is verified by default; Vapi is not unless you set a secret. See Webhooks & tools.

docs.title: Vapi
docs.text:
• Base URL https://api.vapi.ai. Agents are "assistants".
  • The system prompt lives inline in model.messages as a system entry.
  • Callee is customer.number; transcript is artifact.transcript.
  • Webhook envelope {"message": {"type": ...}}; call id at message.call.id.

docs.title: Retell
docs.text:
• Base URL https://api.retellai.com, with mixed endpoint prefixes (/create-agent, /v2/create-phone-call, /v3/list-calls).
  • Prompt and greeting live on the separate LLM object referenced by response_engine.llm_id.
  • Callee/caller are to_number / from_number; transcript is transcript.
  • Webhook envelope {"event": ..., "call": {...}}; call id at call.call_id.

Both providers authenticate API requests with Authorization: Bearer <key>.

docs.title: Create a client
docs.text:
Set the provider and its key in the environment and build the client from it:

export VOICE_PROVIDER=vapi        # or retell
export VAPI_API_KEY=...           # or RETELL_API_KEY

from voxbridge import VoiceClient

client = VoiceClient.from_env()

The explicit form takes the same options (see Configuration):

client = VoiceClient(provider="vapi", api_key="sk-...")  # or provider="retell"

Unknown provider names raise ValueError. The client is a context manager and close() runs on exit:

with VoiceClient.from_env() as client:
    ...

docs.title: Create an agent
docs.text:
from voxbridge import Agent, Tool

agent = client.create_agent(Agent(
    name="Scheduler",
    system_prompt="You are a friendly scheduling assistant.",
    model="gpt-4o",
    voice="elevenlabs:rachel",       # "<tts-provider>:<voiceId>"
    first_message="Hi, this is Scheduler. How can I help?",
    tools=[Tool(
        name="book_appointment",
        description="Book an appointment slot",
        parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {"day": {"type": "string"}}},
        endpoint_url="https://example.com/tools/book",
    )],
))
print(agent.id)          # provider-assigned id
print(agent.raw)         # the untouched provider payload

The same Agent works on either provider; voxbridge maps the prompt, voice and tools into each provider's native shape. Voice ids are "<tts-provider>:<voiceId>" (elevenlabs is normalized to 11labs), but the voice catalogs differ between providers, so check the voice exists on the one you use. Retell stores the prompt on a separate LLM object, so create_agent makes two API calls there; see Providers for what that means for updates and failures.

docs.title: Place a call
docs.text:
call = client.create_call(agent.id, "+15550000000", from_number="+15550000001")
call = client.get_call(call.id)
print(call.status, call.transcript)

for c in client.list_calls(limit=20):
    print(c.id, c.status)

Outbound calls need a caller number (from_number) on both providers. Retell raises ValueError without it. On Vapi, pass an E.164 number, looked up among your phone numbers (ProviderError if none matches), or a phone-number id.

docs.title: Handle a webhook
docs.text:
parse_webhook verifies the request and normalizes it to a WebhookEvent. Pass the raw body bytes, not re-serialized JSON:

from voxbridge import CallEnded, ToolCall, TranscriptChunk

event = client.parse_webhook(request.headers, raw_body)
match event:
    case CallEnded(call_id=cid, transcript=t, ended_reason=r):
        ...
    case TranscriptChunk(role=role, text=text):
        ...
    case ToolCall(name=name, arguments=args):
        reply = client.tool_response(event, {"ok": True})  # return as the HTTP 200 JSON body

A failed verification raises SignatureError; a malformed body raises ProviderError. Verification rules differ per provider (Vapi accepts unsigned requests unless you set a secret), so read Webhooks & tools before going to production. A runnable FastAPI server is in examples/fastapi_server.py.

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
Every agent/call method has an a-prefixed async twin with the same signature (parse_webhook, verify_signature and tool_response are sync):

async with VoiceClient.from_env() as client:
    agent = await client.acreate_agent(Agent(
        name="Scheduler", system_prompt="Be brief.", model="gpt-4o", voice="openai:alloy",
    ))
    call = await client.aget_call("call_123")
    calls = await client.alist_calls()

parse_webhook, verify_signature and tool_response stay synchronous; they do no I/O.

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text:
from voxbridge import AuthError, NotSupported, ProviderError, RateLimited

try:
    client.get_call("call_123")
except RateLimited as exc:
    print("retry in", exc.retry_after)
except AuthError:
    print("check your API key")
except ProviderError as exc:
    print(exc.status_code, exc.body)
except NotSupported as exc:
    print("not available on this provider:", exc)

AuthError and RateLimited subclass ProviderError, so catch them first. Each request is retried at most once; see the API reference for the exact policy.

docs.title: Webhooks & tools
docs.text:
Providers push call events and tool invocations to HTTP endpoints you host. voxbridge verifies each request, normalizes it to one WebhookEvent, and builds the reply a tool call needs. The calls are synchronous and do no I/O:

event = client.parse_webhook(headers, raw_body)   # verifies, then parses

Always pass the raw request body bytes. Signatures are computed over the exact bytes the provider sent, so re-serialized JSON will fail verification. client.verify_signature(headers, raw_body) returns a bool if you want to check without parsing.

A runnable FastAPI server that handles both webhooks and tool calls is in examples/fastapi_server.py.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Vapi Retell Verified by default No Yes Mechanism X-Vapi-Secret header equal to your secret, or Authorization: Bearer <secret> x-retell-signature: v={ts},d={hex}, HMAC-SHA256 over raw_body + ts Key used webhook_secret (VAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET) webhook_secret (RETELL_WEBHOOK_SECRET), otherwise the API key Replay protection none (no timestamp) rejects signatures older than webhook_max_age (default 300 s; None disables) Failure SignatureError SignatureError

Vapi webhooks are unsigned unless you set a secret

With no webhook_secret, voxbridge accepts every Vapi request, including forged ones. If you serve tool calls, anyone who finds the URL can run your tools. Always set VAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET (and the matching credential on the Vapi side) in production. Vapi's HMAC credential is not supported in 0.1.0.

Retell: use the webhook-badged key

Retell signs with the API key that has the webhook badge in the Retell dashboard. With no webhook_secret, voxbridge uses api_key, which is correct only if that key is the badged one. Otherwise pass the badged key as webhook_secret.

Passing webhook_max_age for Vapi raises NotSupported.

docs.title: Event mapping
docs.text:
Both providers fold into one union: CallStarted, CallEnded, TranscriptChunk, ToolCall and ErrorEvent. Every event has call_id, provider and the full payload under raw.

Event Vapi message.type Retell event CallStarted status-update (any status except ended) call_started CallEnded end-of-call-report; status-update with ended call_ended, call_analyzed TranscriptChunk transcript transcript_updated (newest turn) ToolCall tool-calls a custom-function request (name, args, call) ErrorEvent any other type any other event

ErrorEvent is also what you get for event types voxbridge does not map, with the type named in message, so handle it by logging, not by failing the request. Speaker roles are normalized: Retell's agent becomes assistant.

Dedupe on call_id

One call can produce several CallEnded events (Vapi: a status update plus the end-of-call report; Retell: call_ended and the richer call_analyzed). Treat call_id as the idempotency key and keep the event with the transcript.

docs.title: Tool calls
docs.text:
Declare a tool with Tool(..., endpoint_url="https://your.host/tools"), then answer the request your endpoint receives:

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

from voxbridge import SignatureError, ToolCall, VoiceClient

app = FastAPI()
client = VoiceClient.from_env()


@app.post("/tools")
async def tools(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    try:
        event = client.parse_webhook(request.headers, await request.body())
    except SignatureError:
        return JSONResponse({"error": "invalid signature"}, status_code=401)
    if not isinstance(event, ToolCall):
        return JSONResponse({"error": "not a tool call"}, status_code=400)
    result = {"booked": event.arguments.get("day")}
    return JSONResponse(client.tool_response(event, result))   # HTTP 200

Vapi tool endpoints and VAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET

voxbridge registers Vapi tools with server.url only. If your tool endpoint verifies with VAPI_WEBHOOK_SECRET, configure the matching server secret/credential on the assistant or tool in Vapi. An existing one is preserved when voxbridge updates the agent.

ToolCall carries name, arguments (a dict) and tool_call_id. Send the value of client.tool_response(event, result) back as the JSON body with status 200; result must be JSON-serializable.

Vapi Retell Request tool-calls message; tool_call_id is Vapi's id POST {"name", "args", "call"}; tool_call_id is None Reply body {"results": [{"toolCallId": ..., "result": "..."}]} the result itself Result format a single-line string: non-strings are compact-JSON encoded, newlines become spaces a dict stays a JSON object (Retell can map it to response variables); other values are returned as-is

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Vapi, multiple tool calls in one message: only the first is surfaced as the ToolCall; the rest stay in event.raw.
  • Retell args_at_root (a tool option that sends the bare arguments as the body) is not supported, because such a body cannot be told apart from any other payload. Leave it off.
  • Retell result size: Retell truncates tool results at 15,000 characters by default. voxbridge documents this but does not enforce it.
  • Vapi HMAC credentials are not supported; use the shared secret or Bearer form.
  • Malformed bodies (not UTF-8 JSON, not a JSON object, or fields of the wrong type) raise ProviderError, never a bare decode or attribute error.
